prerequisites: Basic formulation and nomenclature of organic and inorganic compounds.
Balancing chemical equations and simple stoichiometric calculations.
Ways to express solution concentration and associated stoichiometric calculations.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and aptitudes in the field of Organization Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment, and solidarity spirit.
Ability to work in a team.
Ability to understand and apply the principles of basic knowledge of general chemistry, organic and inorganic chemistry, and their applications in engineering.
Consolidate knowledge of the fundamentals of chemical terminology, nomenclature, conventions, and units.
Relate macroscopic properties to those of the atoms and molecules constituting matter.
Identify the characteristics of the different states of aggregation.
Describe the types of chemical reactions and their associated main characteristics.
Solve quantitative and qualitative problems according to previously developed models.
Apply the principles of thermodynamics and their applications in Chemistry.
Recognize and value chemical processes in daily life.
Relate Chemistry to other disciplines.
Develop critical reasoning.
Learn autonomously.
Acquire ability to evaluate, interpret and synthesize chemical information.
Work in a team.
Demonstrate and fluently use basic knowledge of Chemistry.
Propose and solve basic problems in the field of Chemistry.
Correctly use the basic terminology employed in the field of chemistry, expressing ideas with precision, being able to establish relationships between different concepts.
Apply the techniques used in a basic chemistry laboratory, including necessary calculations and expressing results appropriately.
Prepare and correctly present reports, both orally and in writing, corresponding to the laboratory practices carried out in the Chemistry course.

syllabus_topics: Object of Chemistry and its relation to other sciences.
Meaning of chemical formulas and chemical nomenclature.
Formulation and nomenclature of simple inorganic and organic compounds.
Amount of substance, mole, and Avogadro's number.
General properties of states of matter.
First principle of Thermodynamics: basic concepts.
Entropy and the second and third principles of Thermodynamics.
Control of reaction rate: influence of concentration and temperature.
Chemical equilibrium in a reaction between gases.
Control of chemical equilibrium and Le Châtelier's principle.
pH and dissociation constants of acids and bases.
Standard reduction potentials and electrochemical series.
assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum score of 4 out of 10 must be obtained in each evaluable aspect (P1, P2, PA, TG, PL seguimiento, PL prueba escrita). The weighted sum of the evaluable aspects must be equal to or greater than 5 out of 10. If the first partial exam is not taken or a minimum of 4 is not achieved, the final exam (E Final) will account for 60% of the grade, with a minimum of 4 required. For extraordinary calls, a minimum of 5 out of 10 is required for both the global exam (E Final) and the average of the laboratory practical parts (PL seguimiento and PL prueba escrita).
